subject: Model shortlist & peak-window profile for onboarding
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@solstice.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 13:14:00 -0000
Subject: Kickoff prep — model shortlist & peak windows

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move from evaluation to an implementation plan and want to align on the initial model candidates and what our peak traffic looks like so CS can finalize the scope. High-level asks from our side:

- A short list of 2–3 model variants you'd recommend for our use case (assistant + retrieval augmented generation).
- Context length trade-offs: minimal acceptable vs recommended for best user UX.
- Ballpark token volumes for average and peak windows so we can plan cost/commitments.

Quick background: our production traffic is expected to be bursty — 10k daily active users but concentrated during 12:00–14:00 PT and 20:00–22:00 PT. Average query length today is ~220 words (prompt+context) with generation averaging ~250 tokens. We expect to ramp after launch, so planning for a 3x–4x surge in the first 6 weeks would be realistic.

Could you share a one-page recommendation and any supporting attachments ahead of a sync tomorrow afternoon? If useful, copy Ben for capacity/throughput comments.

Appreciate it — Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Onboarding, Solstice AI

Attachment: onboarding_requirements.pdf (referenced)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@solstice.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Kickoff prep — model shortlist & peak windows

Evan — thanks for the clear asks and the traffic sketch. I pulled together an initial recommendation and a compact "peak-window profile" that maps model choices to latency/cost/peak throughput assumptions. See attached: model_shortlist.csv and peak_window_profile.xlsx. Summary here so it's searchable in the thread: 

Model shortlist (initial nominees and why)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4_0): best balance for low-latency retrieval-augmented calls, excellent instruction following, low token cost per generation. Good baseline for ~4k context.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8/quantized): stronger multi-turn coherence when you need longer context (~8k). Higher GPU memory but better for multi-prompt flows where you keep more history.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (off-peak variant, float16): for high-quality long-form summarization and occasional heavy generations in off-peak windows; recommend routing only during non-peak or to dedicated capacity.

Context guidance
- Minimal acceptable: 2048 tokens for quality retrieval + short system/prompt. That will handle most Q&A cases.
- Recommended for production UX: 4096 tokens for multi-turn product walkthroughs and documents up to ~3–4k tokens.
- Heavy/document mode: 16k when doing large-document summarization; should be on a separate route or scheduled as batch/off-peak.

Token-volume estimate (your numbers + our adjusted assumptions)
- Current average RTT: prompt ~300 tokens, generation ~250 tokens => ~550 tokens/request.
- Expected day-one load: 10k DAU \u00d7 0.3 calls/user = 3k calls/day => ~1.65M tokens/day baseline.
- Peak window (12:00–14:00 PT, concentrated): assume 40% of daily calls in 2-hour window => 1.2k calls in peak window => ~660k tokens over 2 hours (~5.5k tokens/min).
- Ramp-safe planning (3.5x surge): plan for ~5.8M tokens/day and ~2.3M tokens peak-window.

Operational recommendations
- Start on hosted API with model-tier routing rules; enable prefix caching and a 200ms cold-start SLO.
- For initial weeks, keep Mistral-Instruct as default route; Llama-2-13B-chat as "long context" route that triggers when doc-length > 2.5k tokens.
- Use automatic KV cache for repeated preambles (saves ~18–25% token cost on chat flows).
- If your peak-window budget is strict, reserve a small Dedicated pool for peak 2-hour bursts (fast failover to hosted if capacity shortfall).

I've attached a short CSV with the model variants and estimated per-1k-token cost at our current hosted rates; Ben will add notes on throughput headroom and batching. Happy to hop on a 30-min alignment call tomorrow.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: model_shortlist.csv, peak_window_profile.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@solstice.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Kickoff prep — model shortlist & peak windows

Adding a quick capacity perspective from infra:

- With the 5.8M tokens/day ramp target and ~550 tokens/request avg, you're looking at ~10.5k requests/day. For the 2-hour peak-window projection (~2.3M tokens in peak), that's ~4.2k rps-minutes over 120 minutes => ~35 rps sustained for the peak window.
- If most of your peak traffic hits Mistral-Instruct-7B (our default), a single 8-GPU dedicated pool (A100-style) with batching tuned to 60–80ms tail latency should handle that peak with room.
- KV/prefix cache will reduce compute by ~20% for repeated system prompts. Also recommend request-level batching for the peak window (aggregate small requests into micro-batches of 8–16 depending on latency SLO).

Operational asks for Solstice before we finalize sizing:
1) Can you confirm current average tokens/request and 95th percentile request size?
2) Do you expect document-upload summarization jobs to run during the same peak windows or only off-peak?
3) Any compliance constraints that require Private deployment for initial rollout?

If you can share (1) and (2) prior to the call we'll firm up whether hosted capacity is sufficient or if we should propose a short-term Dedicated commit.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan@solstice.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Kickoff prep — model shortlist & peak windows

Thanks, Grace and Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers below before our sync: 

1) Current telemetry (pre-launch): avg tokens/request ~560, 95th ~1,200 tokens (when users paste longer docs).
2) Document summarization: most customers trigger it off a button; for our beta we expect ~15% of requests to be doc-summarization and they'll generally happen outside the 12:00–14:00 PT peak, but evening window (20:00–22:00 PT) may include some.
3) No hard compliance blockers for hosted in the beta; we'll escalate if SOC2 evidence is required for the GA contract.

Next steps: please finalize the one-pager with per-model latency and cost bands and mark any models that should be scheduled to "off-peak" only. We'll confirm a time for the 30-min alignment call tomorrow at 14:30 PT if that works for the Redwood team.

— Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Onboarding, Solstice AI
